classification.difficultyReason: Recognise the electron count as hydrogen mass divided by electron mass, calculate the scientific-notation ratio and round to a whole number.

content.prompt: The mass of a hydrogen atom is approximately $1.674\times10^{-27}$ kg and the mass of an electron is approximately $9.1\times10^{-31}$ kg. How many electrons, correct to the nearest whole number, will it take to equal the mass of a single hydrogen atom?

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}N&=\frac{1.674\times10^{-27}}{9.1\times10^{-31}}\\N&=\frac{1.674}{9.1}\times10^4\\N&=\frac{167400}{91}\\N&\approx1840\end{align*}$$

Approximately 1840 electrons have the mass of one hydrogen atom.
